title: Drum Handling
intro: Recommended practices for lifting, moving and storing cable reels — wrong methods versus correct methods.

blocks.caption: Do not lift by top flange; cable or reel will be damaged.

blocks.alt: Correct — cradle both reel flanges between forks
blocks.caption: Cradle both reel flanges between forks.

blocks.alt: Incorrect — hoisting without a spreader bar
blocks.caption: Use a spreader bar to prevent bending the reel flanges and mashing the cable.

blocks.alt: Correct — hoist with shaft through both flanges
blocks.caption: Reels can be hoisted with a shaft extended through both flanges.

blocks.alt: Incorrect — upended heavy reels without inspection
blocks.caption: Upended heavy reels will often arrive damaged. Refuse or receive subject to inspection for hidden damage.

blocks.alt: Correct — place spacers under flanges for fork access
blocks.caption: Place spacers under the bottom flange and between reels to create a space to insert the forks.

blocks.alt: Correct — lower reels carefully with hydraulic gate, hoist or fork lift
blocks.caption: Lower reels from truck using hydraulic gate, hoist or fork lift. Lower carefully.

blocks.alt: Incorrect — fork tynes touching cable surface
blocks.caption: Never allow fork tynes to touch cable surface or reel wrap.

blocks.alt: Correct — load with flanges on edge and chock securely
blocks.caption: Always load with flanges on edge and chock and block securely.
